# Phase 02 — task ledger

One row per task. **Status values:** `DONE` (implemented and verified by something executed) ·
`IN PROGRESS` · `TODO` · `BLOCKED` (a genuine external blocker, named) · `NOT STARTED`.

`DONE` never means "written". It means a command was run and its output is recorded in
[`PHASE-02-TEST-EVIDENCE.md`](PHASE-02-TEST-EVIDENCE.md).

Decision IDs follow the Master Product Plan / Decision Register v1.0 (2026-10-14). Where a task
implements a design decision this repository made rather than one the register fixes, the design
document is cited instead — inventing a register ID would be worse than citing nothing.

(2) `title` and the visually-hidden label were left exactly as rendered, so after adding a page the accessible name still read *"Add :page to favourites"* while `aria-pressed` beside it said `true` — **the control stated the opposite of its own state**. Plus nothing was announced between click and answer. All copy travels in the markup (`data-ss-fav-title-on/off`, `-label-on/off`, `-text-on/off`, `data-ss-favourite-busy`), which is that partial's own stated convention — *"so the JS holds no URLs or copy"* — and the fix reuses `announceLive()` rather than adding a second notification mechanism. **MY OWN TEST WAS INVALID FIRST, AND THAT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** It routed `**/favourite*`, which does **not** match `/merchant-favourite-page` — the segment starts with `merchant-`. Neither interception ever fired, so both clicks hit the real server: the SUCCESS assertions passed **by coincidence** (the server's own toggle produced the same answer the fake body would have) and the FAILURE phase never failed, reporting `false -> true`. Every interception is counted and asserted now, so a pattern matching nothing fails loudly. A second assertion was weak in the same way: it claimed *"it was announced"* while the region still held the **busy** text, so it could not tell the busy and error messages apart; it waits for the error string read from the markup. And a third: sampling the live region the instant `aria-busy` appeared always read empty, because `announceLive()` blanks the region and fills it on a 50 ms timeout — that blank frame is deliberate, so two identical messages are both audible. |

So this row is not a fix; it is the thing that stops the next contributor undoing one, which is what its acceptance asks for in as many words ("a ratchet that fails on a new one"). The same lesson this phase has now met four times: an unasserted property is one edit away from an absent one, and P2-04-10 found four places where that had already happened. <br><br>**22 PROPERTIES ARE CHECKED, AND `top`/`bottom` DELIBERATELY ARE NOT.** They do not flip with writing direction in any locale this product ships, so rewriting them would be churn with no reader who benefits. The pairs that ARE checked are the ones that paint the wrong edge in exactly one of the two builds — the hardest kind of defect to notice, because the build in front of you is usually the right one. <br><br>**THE DETECTOR HAS ITS OWN PREMISE TEST**, because every assertion here is satisfied by a detector that matches nothing: it is handed a string that must trip it and a logical one that must not. And **comments are blanked before scanning** — a lesson this repository has paid for twice: a source-text scanner that does not strip comments matches its own prose, so a file explaining why it avoids `margin-left` would fail a test looking for `margin-left`. Blanked rather than deleted, so the reported line numbers still point at the real lines. <br><br>**STATED LIMIT:** this covers `store-syria-ds.css` only, which is the row's wording. No blur-and-refocus trick either — the second focus would be PROGRAMMATIC and `:focus-visible` does not apply to that, so the measurement would have destroyed the thing it measures. **AND A SECOND FALSE READING:** the palette's input appeared in the tab order while the palette was shut. Two of those bites did not bite at first and the fix was to the TEST, not the bite: the disclosure case reads `Artisan::output()`, so a leak written with `echo` was invisible to it. The claim is now carried by a pair — the output case plus a channel census asserting the command contains no `Log::`, `echo`, `var_dump`, `print_r`, `fwrite`, `dd(`, `dump(` or `error_log` — because S4 is a token reaching a **log**, which the output case cannot see. **AND THE MANDATED REVIEW FOUND A LIVE DEFECT IN THE INSTRUMENT ITSELF — a correctness one, not a disclosure one; it was clean on every credential, authorization and tenancy question it was asked.** The command paged with `chunk()`, i.e. `LIMIT n OFFSET m`. The interference I had reasoned about was the wrong one: `CustomAuth:88`'s `UPDATE` of `last_used_at` **cannot** disturb offset paging, because it cannot move a row within `ORDER BY id`. **Deletes can**, and this table is deleted from constantly — *every login revokes first*, `$user->tokens()->delete()` at ten call sites (merchant login, driver login, customer login, three logouts, three password resets) — and each delete below the offset shifts the window and skips exactly one row. The error direction is the bad one: the skipped row can be the single oldest in-use token, so the under-count makes a **shorter expiry look safer than it is**. Now `chunkById()`, keyset paging, which also removes the `O(N²/1000)` offset re-traversal on a table nothing prunes. **Driven**, not source-asserted: the page size is shrunk to 2 on the registered command instance and a `DB::listen` hook deletes the lowest id after the first page — the interleave a login produces — and the row offset paging loses is the 900-day one, so the gate reads **900 days keyset, 10 days offset**. **TWO MORE THE REVIEW WAS RIGHT ABOUT.** The gate said *"has ever been presented"* while its own docblock claimed *"is still in use"*: a token last seen 380 days ago is as unheld as one never used, and an orphan (tokenable deleted, refused at `CustomAuth:72`) can never be presented again yet still pinned the maximum — conservative, so not dangerous, but a reader could not tell an inflated bound from a live constraint. The gate now carries the dormancy of the token that set it. And the gate could not answer the question the rollout actually turns on, being a maximum with no cardinality over a distribution that includes never-used tokens; the report now states **per principal how many in-use tokens the owner's approved 30 days would have refused**, which is the figure a rollout is decided on. **ONE CLAIM OF MINE IT FALSIFIED:** the census docblock said *"the console is the only channel"*, and that is false independently of the command's source — a throw reaches `laravel.log` through the exception handler. Nothing sensitive can get there, for two reasons now written down instead of assumed (the `token` column is never selected, and the query's only bindings are the paging integers), and the census is now described as what it is: a ratchet over one file. Its list was also wrong in both directions — `printf` matched the `sprintf()` used for column alignment, and a bare `info(` would have matched `$this->info()`, which **is** the console — so channels are matched as whole calls now. **Final evidence: 13 cases, 13 bites, every one bit**; `tests/Feature/Security` **4272 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed**. <br><br>**[2026-10-30] §5 ACCURACY PASS — THE STATUS WORD `PARTIAL` IS RIGHT; ONE CLAIM IN THE SUPPORTING TEXT IS NOW FALSE, AND STAGE 2's COMPLETED HALF IS UNRECORDED.** **(1) A NOW-FALSE CLAIM.** The row says token lifetime and the absent refresh path *"remain exactly as `P01-TOKEN-EXPIRY-PROPOSAL.md` describes — Sanctum tokens never expire, **every one carries `['*']`**, and there is no refresh for any client."* The `['*']` clause stopped being true when Stage 2 landed, and I re-measured it: **all five mint sites now pass an explicit ability** — `Api\AuthController:316`, `:398`, `:619` pass `['storefront']`; `Api\DashboardController:947` passes `['merchant']`; `:5091` passes `['delivery']`. The accurate sentence is: *"Sanctum tokens never expire and there is no refresh for any client; tokens minted before Stage 2 carry `['*']`, and no route enforces abilities, so the narrowing changes no decision yet."* The "never expire" and "no refresh" clauses are still true and stay. **(2) STAGE 2's MINT HALF IS DONE, TESTED, AND APPEARS NOWHERE IN `docs/`.** The enforce half is deliberately not wired, per the proposal's own *mint first, enforce later*: `CheckAbilities` is imported at `routes/api.php:9` and used on **zero** routes, and `tokenCan()` is called **nowhere** in `app/` — both re-measured. Evidence is `tests/Feature/Security/TokenAbilitiesTest.php`, 10 cases, which no document references. **(3) A STALE CITATION IN THE ONE SENTENCE THAT IS AN INSTRUCTION.** The row says *"the stage-3 target, at `:846`, not the `:687` the proposal names"* — the merchant mint site is **`DashboardController:947`**; `:846` is `$store = Store::find($currentstore);`. Rendering them as stages would assert a delivery stage that does not exist; dropping them would hide live orders from the screen the merchant is on. They are grouped below the board, labelled *"recorded in the same field, but not fulfilment stages"*, and both failure modes are asserted. An unrecognised tenth status also appears rather than vanishing. **THREE DEFECTS THE BROWSER FOUND THAT NO TEST WOULD HAVE, each fixed after being measured:** (1) the flex row's intrinsic width widened its ancestors instead of scrolling inside them — the document measured 2022px against a 1400px viewport and 2066px on a 390px phone, while the order detail page measured the same way did not overflow at all, which is how it was attributed here rather than assumed pre-existing; `min-width: 0` and `max-width: 100%` on the scroller plus a `min-width: 0` wrapper fixed it. (2) The card's buyer name and total read 3.42:1 in dark. Changing the token did nothing, and **raising the DS selector's specificity also did nothing** — because the host's dark stylesheet carries `… , p { color: #808191 !important }`, i.e. EVERY paragraph in the dark admin, which no component CSS can override. Fixed by using `<div>`, which that rule does not match; the theme-wide defect is recorded as **F152** rather than worked around in silence. (3) My own overflow check was wrong — it read the root's `scrollWidth`, which reflects a descendant scroller's extent, and reported an overflow after the fix had already worked; corrected to "is any element wider than the viewport". **Two ratchets caught the slice and were satisfied rather than relaxed:** `ArabicUiCoverageTest` named nine untranslated strings, and `OrderActionPermissionCensusTest` required the new route to be censused. **AMENDED [2026-10-28], P2-04-12: this slice shipped the board with NO ENTRY POINT** — the route was declared and no view linked to it, so it was reachable only by typing the URL, and all twelve tests above call `route('order.kanban')` directly so none of them could notice. Recorded as **F155** and fixed: a *Board View* control in the `action-button` header of both the list and the grid, carrying `request()->query()`, with three tests that assert reachability from the RENDERED pages rather than from a constructed route. Without it an unpermitted employee fills the entire form and is turned away at submit. <br><br>**THREE FLAWS IN MY OWN CENSUS, EACH CAUGHT BEFORE IT COST ANYTHING, AND ONE NEARLY HID THE WRITE HOLE.** (a) `str_contains($action, 'OrderController@')` also matched `DeliverySyriaOrderController@`, so the first run reported a route from another controller; it compares the exact class now. (b) Both `{id}` rows were **vacuous**: `order_view` decrypts its parameter while `order_preview` requires a raw integer and 404s on anything else **before** its permission check — so every case on those rows 404'd for every principal and "refused", "served" and "operator locked out" were indistinguishable. A premise test now fails if any censused URI answers 404 for a permitted holder. (c) My first guard census reported `store()` **absent** because the grep pattern assumed four-space indentation and `store()` is declared at column 1 — so the most serious finding of the row was nearly missed through a flaw in the tool, not the reasoning. <br><br>**NINE EXISTING TESTS WENT RED ACROSS TWO ROUNDS, AND NONE WAS SUPPRESSED.** Five assert the STORE PREDICATE does not refuse the owner (`AdminApiSurfaceTest`, `ApiStoreOwnershipPredicateTest`) and four assert the STOCK contract (`AdminApiStockRefusalContractTest`, `AdminApiOrderStockOwnershipTest`) — all nine drive these endpoints with a fixture merchant who holds **no Laratrust role at all**, so a permission gate made them fail for an orthogonal reason and each would have stopped isolating what it was written for. Their fixtures grant the gated permissions now, with the reason written into every file. A real merchant is unaffected: the shared global `admin` role carries them and every merchant is given it for every store. <br><br>**AND `SecurityLogInventoryTest` WENT RED TWICE, for a reason worth recording:** it keys an observability inventory by `file:line`, and editing `OrderController` shifted **ten** log statements — then shifted them again when the prose was corrected. The numbers are **derived** from each message's actual position now rather than hand-patched, and regenerating that inventory is the last step before committing a change to a file it indexes. <br><br>**AND THE FULL GATE CAUGHT WHAT MY SUBSET DID NOT.** `638d06c1` was pushed as verified and the full Feature run then returned **12 failed, 3 errored** — ten of them mine, all in `tests/Feature/Commerce/OrderStoreOwnershipTest`, with `no such table: permissions`. That directory **builds its own schema** because `RefreshDatabase` cannot run the full migration set on SQLite, so it creates only the tables "this writer actually touches" — and gating `store()` made the writer touch two more. The errors matter more than the failures: the gate holds errors at a zero baseline because a test that could not run is worse than one whose assertion failed. **The process error is the part worth keeping:** I derived the suite set from the suites I already knew about rather than from what the changed code is driven by, so a 4414-test regression looked thorough while omitting the one suite dedicated to the handler I changed. `grep -rl OrderController tests/` would have found it in one command. It cannot express *confirm, then resubmit this AJAX form with one extra key*. P2-01-19's own test file contains no nesting clause at all. **[2026-10-30] BUILT AND VERIFIED UNDER §4.4. F184 IS NOW IMPLEMENTED ON EVERY FIRST-PARTY DOOR.** Both blockers were cleared first — F196 made the Save path's *"Nothing has been changed"* true, and F195 put one policy on every door — so the dialog is now a confirmation of a refusal that really is a refusal. **What shipped.** A DS dialog primitive (`StoreSyriaDS.openDialog` / `closeDialog` / `confirmDestructive`, `public/js/store-syria-ds.js`) rendering the `.ss-dialog` CSS family that had existed since the DS was written and **had never been rendered by anything** — first use, not composition; a Blade shell (`components/ss/confirm-dialog.blade.php`); one shared bridge (`product/_variant-delete-dialog.blade.php`) included by **both** the editor and the read-only SHOW screen, which also carries live trash buttons; the trash-click gate in both variant panels; and the Save path's refusal dialog. Every string already existed in both `ar.json` and `en.json` — no new key. **The consent signal is verifiable, not decorative.** The merchant's client echoes the **variant name** back (`ss_confirm_variant` on the trash door, `confirm_variant` on the API door) and the server compares it to the stored name, so a hand-posted DELETE with `confirm=1` is refused: *"a parameter was set"* is not *"someone saw what they were deleting"*. Measured by reverting the two guards to the pre-F184 hardcoded `true` — **4 of the 6 consent cases fail**; the 2 that still pass are the hard-block cases, which by design refuse regardless of consent. **THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW FOUND A DEFECT INSIDE THIS CHANGE, AND IT WAS THE SIGNAL'S USABILITY.** `VariantRemovalPolicy::refuse()` hardcoded `'confirm_with' => 'ss_confirm_variant_removal'` — the **bulk** door's key, whose value is a boolean — while the two per-variant doors read different keys and want the variant name; and `DeleteVariant()` forwards that array to the client verbatim. An API client that followed the hint would have been refused for ever, reading as a server bug rather than a consent requirement. `refuse()` now takes the calling door's consent descriptor (`['key' => …, 'value' => 'variant_name']`, defaulting to the bulk door so no existing call site moved) and advertises `confirm_value` too — and a `confirm_value` is advertised **only** when exactly one variant is named, because advertising the first of several would invite a client to confirm one and delete the rest. The test does not merely match the strings: it sends the advertised pair back and asserts the delete then succeeds. **Browser evidence: 229 checks across FIVE configurations, 0 failures** (`docs/development/phase-2/evidence/f184/f184-browser-5-configs.txt`), by a harness committed as `docs/development/phase-2/tools/check-f184-confirmation.cjs` and re-run from the repository to prove it reproduces. The fifth configuration is the trap this row's recon named: **an Arabic store with `SITE_RTL` off**, because direction comes from the per-store setting and not from the locale, so `[dir="rtl"]` never matches there. Proven in all five: the click opens the dialog instead of deleting (no DELETE is sent); the dialog names the variant and states the loss is permanent; `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"`; focus lands on **Cancel**, not on the destroying button; Escape is Cancel and sends nothing; Cancel sends nothing; Confirm sends **exactly one** DELETE carrying the consent echo; all five contrast ratios ≥ 4.5:1 in light and dark; the dialog fits a 390px viewport. And §4.3 holds in the browser, not just in PHPUnit: **a CONFIRMED delete of an order-blocked variant left every card in the DOM**, refused with a 409, and the refusal reached the merchant both visibly and in the assertive live region — while on an order-free product the same confirmed delete removed exactly one card. **TWO MEASUREMENTS CORRECTED MY OWN WORK HERE.** (1) The accordion kept toggling open behind the backdrop in every configuration. (c) **Disable model caching** (`MODEL_CACHE_ENABLED=false`): one setting, removes the defect outright, costs whatever the caching was buying, which is unmeasured here. The owner's §2.5 asks for configuration and documentation prepared for testing without assuming production availability, so the activation order is a runbook (`docs/development/phase-2/F194-MODEL-CACHE-ISOLATION-RUNBOOK.md`): migrate, verify the tables, set the variable, clear the **compiled config** (not `cache:clear`), verify. Recorded so the owner can choose it knowingly if the deployment is single-node. **Evidence — `tests/Support/Security/bin/verify-model-cache-isolation-on-mysql.php`, 16 checks, 0 failures on MariaDB 10.11.14 with the database store:** the two store classes really do differ in taggability (the mechanism); the application and model stores are the **same driver** and **different tables**; a **full flush of the model store** leaves all five seeded payment keys; `Setting::updateOrCreate()`, `::create()`, `::save()`, `::delete()` and an explicit `flushCache()` each leave them; and the model cache serves the **new** value after a write and a flush, which is D-28a's no-stale-reads condition. **Section F deliberately shows an explicit flush of the APPLICATION store still erasing all five**, so a green run cannot be read as *the payment cache is safe*. **Plus `tests/Unit/Security/ModelCacheIsolationConfigTest.php`, 4 cases, 3 bites every one bit** — the model store sharing the application table · activation by default · model caching disabled. It reads the config **files** rather than booting the application, because a stale `bootstrap/cache/config.php` can fool a booted read, which happened for real in this session (see F197). Compared with `hash_equals`, because this one IS a secret — unlike the per-variant name echo, which a caller is *supposed* to be able to read off the row. **A SERVER-HELD RECORD, NOT A SIGNATURE, AND THERE IS NO HONEST ALTERNATIVE.** `APP_KEY` is in git history and unrotated — this repository already records that as why `Crypt::encrypt()` is an encoding; `URL::temporarySignedRoute` derives from the same key and has no first-party use; every first-party `hash_hmac` is keyed on a payment gateway's secret. The one sound HMAC primitive lives in a vendored package and reads a master secret `config/` does not hold for app code. So the secret is the stored record, as `OrderCompleteBinding` already decided for order ids — and a stateless signature could not be **consumed**, which is what stops a captured token authorising a second removal. **WHERE IT LIVES IS A DEPLOYMENT DECISION AND IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN.** NOT the default cache store: `laravel-model-caching` flushes on every model save, and because `DatabaseStore` is not taggable that flush is `Cache::flush()` over the **whole** store — one `Setting::updateOrCreate()` erased 4 of 4 seeded keys on MariaDB in this repository's own script, and `Product` and `ProductVariant` are both `Cachable`. `config/consent.php` names the store, defaulting to `file`, which a default-store flush does not touch — asserted, not assumed. **The residual: a file-backed record is per-server**, so a multi-server deployment without sticky sessions can issue on one machine and verify on another. Set `CONSENT_STORE` to a shared store where one exists; the alternatives are activating `MODEL_CACHE_STORE=model_cache` (F194's runbook) or a dedicated table — **a persistent migration, which is an owner escalation**. Nothing here touches production. **A SEPARATE FIELD, NOT THE OLD ONE, AND THAT WAS A TRAP WORTH AVOIDING:** all three server reads were `$request->boolean()`, and `filter_var('9f3ac1…', FILTER_VALIDATE_BOOLEAN)` is **false** — so putting a token in `ss_confirm_variant_removal` would have silently turned every confirmed save into an unconfirmed one while twelve tests posting `1` carried on passing. **A TEST FOUND A REAL DESIGN GAP:** binding the token to one path's removal set broke a request carrying BOTH a choice set and an attribute set — the retry verified against the choice path, matched, and was then refused by the attribute path, whose set the token did not cover. The token now binds the **union**, which is also the honest reading of *"the variant IDs that will be deleted"*: what the merchant agrees to is the effect of the whole request. **THE CONCURRENCY CONDITION, MEASURED ON TWO REAL CONNECTIONS** (`tests/Support/Security/bin/verify-variant-removal-consent-on-mysql.php`, **8 checks, 0 failures**, MariaDB 10.11.14). The owner's words were *"do not claim the operation is safe on the strength of a sequential test alone"*, and the suite runs on SQLite where `lockForUpdate()` **compiles to nothing** — so a PHPUnit case asserting this would pass whether or not the protection existed. Measured instead: **[2] the race is real** — the unprotected shape checked, saw 0 references, a cart row landed from another connection, and the variant was deleted under it; **[3] the lock holds** — with `deleteGuarded()`'s `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` taken first, the concurrent INSERT **blocked for 2.00s and timed out** instead of slipping through; **[4] and a referenced variant survives** — the guard refuses and deletes nothing, which is the owner's *"stop the dangerous delete rather than treating it as safe"*. The lock is on the **reference** rows rather than the variants, because the dangerous write is a cart row arriving, not a variant changing — locking the variants would serialise two merchants editing one product and still let the cart row land. **CONSENT STILL CANNOT OVERRIDE A D-20 HARD BLOCK**, and it holds by construction rather than by call-site care: `refuse()` reads `$confirmed` at exactly one place, after every reference check. A token is issued **only** for the consent branch — a refusal carrying `blocked` gets none, because handing one over would tell the merchant they could proceed by confirming when they cannot. **EVIDENCE:** `VariantRemovalConsentTest` 15 cases; every binding bitten — dropping the id sort fails 2, dropping the state hash fails 5, dropping single use fails 1, making every binding inert fails 6. The end-to-end case `test_the_old_boolean_alone_no_longer_authorises_a_removal` drives `'1'`, `'true'`, `'yes'` and `'on'` through the real route and asserts **no variant is deleted** — and restoring `$request->boolean()` in the preflight fails 5 tests. Twelve test sites that posted the boolean now do the real round trip (refuse → read the advertised pair → send it back), which asserts something the literal never could: **that what the server advertises is what the server accepts**. |
| **F206** | **F195 turned a dead operator exemption into a live capability: the platform operator can now edit ANY store's product through the merchant web `update()` door.** Found on the final gate by `verify-product-ownership-on-mysql.php`, which had asserted the opposite and failed — the only failure in the 27-script MariaDB roster, and it was a stale expectation rather than a broken fix. **Mechanism:** `update()`'s body sat inside `if ($actor->isAbleTo('Edit Products'))`, and CLAUDE.md's standing rule is that `isAbleTo()` alone **refuses the platform operator** (Laratrust has no super-admin bypass). So the operator never reached the ownership guard, and the `UserPolicy::PLATFORM_ADMIN` exemption written INTO that guard — whose own comment says it matches `OrderPolicy::allow` — was defence in depth that could not fire. F195 replaced the gate with `MerchantPermissions::allowsAny($actor, ['Edit Products'], $product->store_id)` because `isAbleTo()` resolves through `allPermissions()` with **no store predicate** and is a union across every store: it answers the wrong question for a merchant and refuses the operator. `MerchantPermissions` answers per-store and gives the operator the `['*']` wildcard the operator-first rule requires. The exemption therefore became reachable. | **INTENDED, BUT SURFACED FOR THE OWNER RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE INFERRED FROM A GREEN RUN.** It is what the code was written to do, it matches `OrderPolicy`, and it is what the owner's own §4.2 case list asks for — the platform operator is named there as a principal that must be resolved, and `test_the_platform_operator_can_still_delete_a_product_variant` asserts the operator CAN act on the variant doors. The pre-F195 refusal was the defect. **But it widens what a platform operator can do on a merchant's catalogue, and that deserves to be stated, not discovered.** The MariaDB script now asserts the new behaviour with the whole account in its own comment (16 checks, 0 failures), and names it a capability change rather than letting a green run imply nothing moved. `show()` and `edit()` are unchanged — they never had an `isAbleTo` wrapper, so the exemption was always live there. **If the owner does not want the operator editing merchant catalogues, say so and it becomes a one-line narrowing** — but it would then also have to be narrowed on the variant doors, where the owner's directive explicitly asked for the opposite. **[2026-10-30] OWNER DECIDED, AND IMPLEMENTED: THE PLATFORM OPERATOR READS A MERCHANT'S CATALOGUE AND DOES NOT WRITE IT.** The owner's words: the operator may read and diagnose, but may not edit a merchant's products, prices, stock or variants, nor delete them, absent explicit and specific delegation; and *"do not invent a new delegation system — if no suitable mechanism exists, block the write for now and document what delegation would require."* **THE FIRST PLAN WAS WRONG AND RECON CAUGHT IT.** I was going to narrow `MerchantPermissions::allowsAny()`. That helper gates **2 of the 13** reachable doors. The operator reaches a merchant's catalogue through **five** mechanisms: (A) the `['*']` wildcard plus an ownership exemption — `ProductController::update`, `Api::DeleteVariant`, and via `VariantRemovalPolicy::authorize`'s own operator limb `Api::UpdateVariant` and `product_attribute_delete`; (B) **no permission check at all** — `Api::{UpdateProduct, AddProduct, DeleteProduct}`, standing on `resolveOwnedStore()`, which drops its `created_by` predicate for the operator; (C) `lacksProductPermission()` + `productIsOutsideCurrentStore()` — the three media writers; (D) **`BulkDeleteTenantGuard`**, which returned `$next($request)` for the operator *before* its permission map, its model map and its tenant predicate, over a vendored handler whose body is `whereIn('id', $ids)->delete()` with no store predicate — the widest door, and it touches none of the others; (E) `SettingController::currencySettings`, which rewrites **every product price and every variant price in a store**. A fix scoped to (A) would have left eight doors open while reading as complete. **WHAT SHIPPED:** `App\Services\OperatorCatalogueWrite` — a named per-door guard rather than a narrowing of anything shared, because each of the four tempting chokepoints is load-bearing elsewhere: the wildcard also serves orders, coupons, analytics and the Flutter login payload; `resolveOwnedStore()` has 91 call sites across stores, plans, settings, payment credentials and more; the two private helpers are shared with the **read** paths the owner asked to preserve; and `isOperator()` is consumed by eight files, five policies and two Gates. `grep -rn 'OperatorCatalogueWrite::' app/` now lists every governed door, so a new catalogue writer that forgets it is visible as an absence. Nine call sites close thirteen doors — one of them (`VariantRemovalPolicy`) closes four at once, which is what D-28c put the policy there for. Each door refuses in **its own idiom**: `update()` returns the AJAX `flag`/`msg` array because `edit.blade.php` reads it without navigating and a redirect would be a blank toast; the API doors use `error()` (HTTP **200**, `status: 0`) because a new 401 forces a logout in the shipped Flutter app; the bulk guard uses its own `reject()`. **MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER.** Before: the operator's web save returned `{"flag":"success"}` and rewrote the price from 100 to **1**. After: 14 cases pass, and neutering the guard to `return false` fails **8** of them — the seven write doors plus the guard's own test. Controls kept throughout: the merchant still saves, permitted staff still save, a merchant of another store is still refused (F195's tenancy work unmoved), and the operator still **reads** both the web product screen and the Admin API. **THREE OF MY OWN TESTS WERE VACUOUS AND THE REVERT CHECK IS WHAT EXPOSED THEM.** The operator's web-save case passed before the fix because its payload had `cost_price=40` against `price=1` and the rule is `cost_price <= price`, so the **validator** refused before authorization was consulted. `AddProduct` answered HTTP **500** for every principal (`Attempt to read property "max_products" on null` — no plan in the fixture) and my `assertApiRefused` read `(int) null` as `0`, i.e. **accepted a crash as a refusal**; the helper now asserts the status is under 500 first. And the API read tests asserted against a door that 500s for everyone on `currency_rates`, a GATE-F table no migration declares — the suite builds it now, as two sibling suites already do. **THREE EXISTING TESTS ASSERTED THE OLD CAPABILITY AND WERE REWRITTEN, NOT WEAKENED:** `VariantRemovalPolicyTest::test_the_platform_operator_may_delete_a_variant_in_any_store` and `MerchantProductOwnershipTest`'s image and variant pair. Each now asserts the refusal **and** keeps a merchant control that still succeeds, so none can pass by everything being broken. On the trash door the operator now meets **403 before F184's 409** — capability before ceremony, deliberately: a principal who may not delete at all should not be told to confirm first. **WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, AND IT IS NOT A DETAIL.** A delegation mechanism **already exists** — `lab404/laravel-impersonate`, wired through `StoreController::LoginWithAdmin` and `UserPolicy::impersonate` (operator only, refuses self, refuses another operator). So F206's *"if no mechanism exists"* branch does not apply. But after `Impersonate::take()` `auth()->user()` **is the merchant**, so every gate in this codebase — including this one — reads the merchant's identity: **the block stops the operator's direct writes and does not stop operator-via-impersonation writes.** That would be tolerable if impersonation were attributable, and it is not: **no catalogue write is audit-logged anywhere in this application** (`AuditLog::record` covers plan orders, users and password resets; the `ActivityLog` writers are storefront-only). A price edited while impersonating is indistinguishable from the merchant's own. **That is the specification of what delegation would require, and it is the owner's call:** a catalogue audit trail that records actor, impersonator, store, product, field, before and after; a scope on the impersonation grant; and a time bound. **ALSO NOT BLOCKED, BY SCOPE:** product brands and labels (catalogue taxonomy, not products, prices, stock or variants — the operator can still write them through `resolveOwnedStore`-only doors), and `StoreController::ownerstoredestroy`, which is store lifecycle and which the owner excluded. **Catalogue MEDIA was blocked** (`file_delete`, `variant_image_store`, `variant_image_destroy`) — a judgement call, recorded as one: deleting a merchant's image is not diagnosis, and it is a one-line reversal if the owner disagrees. |

## Where these rows came from

40 of the rows below were created on **2026-10-25** by a requirement-by-requirement audit of the
master prompt against this ledger, recorded in
[`PHASE-02-COVERAGE-AUDIT-2026-10-25.md`](PHASE-02-COVERAGE-AUDIT-2026-10-25.md). They carry
`AUDIT-2026-10-25` in their Decisions column and a `REQUIRED:` note in Verified by, because the
evidence they name does not exist yet.

The audit found **31 of the prompt's 104 workstream requirements tracked by no row at all** —
including Workstream J's Reports and Integrations, and all four of Workstream E's order rules. It
also found the coverage check inside the master-prompt document had gone stale. Nothing was
deleted and no status was changed.

Recorded 2026-10-25 from two sources: boundary sentences inside the master prompt itself, which the
coverage audit surfaced, and the owner's scope-separation instruction of the same date. **These are
not tasks. They exist so that work matching them is recognised and declined rather than absorbed.**

| *"Do not implement new Phase 04 product pricing or stock engines in Phase 02."* | master prompt, Workstream D | P2-03-8 and P2-03-9 reorganise and label what exists; they add no pricing or stock logic. |

| **Phase 06 — premium Super Admin UX** | owner instruction, 2026-10-25 | Not started. |

**Standing rule:** do not start Phase 2.5, Phase 03 or Phase 06 during Phase 02 execution.

(5) The operator check used `strtolower(trim(...))`, the exact normalisation `UserPolicy` records as WRONG — MySQL's PAD SPACE folds a trailing space but not a leading one, so `trim()` grants operator status to a row every SQL comparison refuses; `OperatorCheckCensusTest` forbids it but only in three named files, so **CI would not have caught it**. Fixed with `UserPolicy::isOperator()`, deliberately not a literal comparison, which would have pushed the census to 102 against `CEILING = 101`. (6) The recent-pages session key was not keyed to the principal. <br><br>**AND ONE DEFECT THE REVIEW REASONED PAST THAT THE FEATURE SUITE CAUGHT.** `Menu::permits()` calls `isAbleTo()`, which `App\Models\Customer` does not have — so a Customer reaching the directory is a FATAL, and because the middleware runs on every web request that fatal landed on the STOREFRONT: **112 security tests across `OrderDocumentAccessTest`, `StorefrontAccountOwnershipTest` and `StorefrontOrderRefundOwnershipTest` turned 500**. The reasoning that missed it was "`auth()` with no argument is the `web` guard and a customer leaves it empty" — true of `CustomAuth`, false of `actingAs($customer)`, which puts a Customer on `web` because Laravel never type-checks the model against the provider. Fixed with an `instanceof App\Models\User` guard and pinned by a test that reproduces the exception. **Review is not a substitute for running the suite.** <br><br>**OPERATOR ROWS ARE FILED UNDER STORE 1**, recorded rather than left to be discovered: `getCurrentStore()` returns a hardcoded `1` for a `super admin` with no `current_store`. Not a cross-tenant read — every query filters `user_id` AND `store_id` — but their favourites follow whatever store that helper resolves. Also measured: that helper's fallback is `Store::where('created_by', $user->id)`, so a Customer id colliding with a merchant id resolves a real store; nothing is written because the directory gate refuses the page, which is the control of record. <br><br>The toggle lives in the command palette rather than 69 page headers, including vendored screens this project must not edit. `--ss-fg-muted` needed `!important`: the host's `style-dark.css` carries a bare `p { color: #808191 !important }` in a selector list, measured live at 3.85:1 on the sunken surface. **And the live harness itself was measuring the wrong thing twice** — `data-ss-theme` comes from the `cust_darklayout` SETTING, not Playwright's `colorScheme`, so both "light" and "dark" cases ran dark until the premise assertion was added; and "reads correctly in Arabic" was only checking direction and colour until an assertion that the strings are actually translated was added (`__()` falls back to the English key). |

## Escalation list — the owner decisions that currently hold P2-01/P2-03/P2-04 rows shut (2026-10-28)

Measured by reading the code for each row, not inferred from the ledger. Each entry is a decision
only the owner can take under CLAUDE.md §2; none is a question about how to build the thing.

**Four rows need the SAME decision: a persistent migration.** CLAUDE.md §2 reserves those, and
`app/Services/TableFilterMemory.php:16-24` already records why no non-migration storage works — the
four alternatives were each ruled out by measurement, not preference: `settings` cannot hold a
per-employee value because `SettingOwnership` rewrites `created_by` to `$user->creatorId()`, so two
employees of one merchant collapse onto one row; `localStorage` cannot be per-employee without
putting a user id in the DOM, which re-opens P2-06-4's disclosure argument; a cookie name is a
browser-global slot, so the second employee at a shared terminal overwrites the first.

| Row | What it needs | What is already built |
|---|---|---|
| **P2-04-9** saved views | a column or table to store a named filter set | everything else: the `ss_status`/`ss_payment`/`ss_from`/`ss_to` vocabulary, its validation, the receipt UI and the URL round-trip. **The "share" clause is already satisfied** — P2-04-8 made every filter combination a shareable URL. Only *named* and *saved* are open |
| **P2-04-11** manual order entry | `orders.order_source` (or equivalent) to mark an order as manually entered | **two** manual paths are already live, not one: POS (`Route::resource('pos')`, gated `Manage Pos`) and the order form. Neither can be told apart from a storefront order today |

| **P2-04-6** order detail | an author column on `order_notes` | the correctness, accessibility and dark-mode half is done and tested |

It is recorded here and in the register, so P2-04-12's invoice-preview clause is an **authorised exception** rather than an outstanding gap — which is what §4 of CLAUDE.md means by "a verified status or an authorised exception". **Three rows need a SCOPE decision instead.**

- **P2-01-18 quick actions** — which create-actions belong in the command palette. The palette, its
  Ctrl/Cmd+K binding, Favourites, Recents and the search half are all built; what is missing is an

  (nothing destructive in the palette) and that decision should be inherited rather than re-asked.
- **P2-01-19 no nested modal workflows** — the first clause is already satisfied (one universal
  confirmation component, 124 call sites). The second cannot be ratcheted yet because the host theme

  removing the 15 nested dialogs would change the AI content generator's workflow — which pulls
  directly against **P2-01-21's own acceptance** that every `data-ajax-popup` caller keeps working.
  Those two rows contradict each other until the owner says which wins.
- **P2-04-12 printing and export** — the invoice-preview clause is module-owned: its view lives under
  `packages/workdo/AutomaticOrderPrinting/`, which CLAUDE.md §2 and
  `.github/scripts/guard-no-workdo-changes.sh` both forbid editing. Either the clause is out of
  scope under the row's own "where already supported", or it needs a first-party invoice preview.
  Everything else on the row is unblocked.

**And two corrections to the ledger's own numbers, both found by measuring:**

- **P2-01-21 is an undercount.** The row says "~65 screens"; the real figure is **266
  `data-ajax-popup` occurrences across 189 files** — 150 in 102 files under `resources/`. The row is
  otherwise small: what it needs is a repo-wide ratchet, because today the only one is a
  single-screen pilot, so a migration of any other screen can drop a caller silently.
- **P2-03-3's own TODO list is stale.** Of the three items it names, two are DONE in other rows

**P2-04-13 is the cheapest row left and nothing blocks it** — no schema gap, no owner decision, no
device. `x-ss.attention` is already written, tested and in production on the dashboard; the row asks
for a second caller of it. The one genuinely new piece of code is that `return_status` is not
filterable anywhere.

**P2-01-20 is the largest unblocked row, and its cause is one declaration.**
`public/assets/css/style.css:15684-15686` is `*:focus { outline: none; }`, present in **all four**
theme stylesheets the layout swaps between — so every non-design-system control on every admin page,
across all 70 vendored modules, has no visible focus ring. Five design-system surfaces already
manage focus correctly. Removing that declaration is a visual change on every screen in the product,
which is why the row is large rather than trivial.

### Accepted follow-ups from the 2026-10-28 review, not folded into this slice

Each was examined; none is a defect left unrecorded.

- **`getActivePaymentMethods` uses the raw `$storeId` string after validation** rather than
  `$store->id`, at two sites. Benign — `resolveOwnedStore()` has already matched it to an owned
  store and a MySQL-loose `'5abc'` resolves to the same row both times — but the sibling at
  `:6446` uses `$store->id` and the idiom should be one. Cosmetic.
- **Three `markTestSkipped` branches remain in `PaymentTypeDisplayTest`'s picker tests.** They
  convert a route regression into a silent skip. CI catches an undeclared skip in both directions,
  so the blast radius is local runs only — but the same branch on the customer-page test is what
  would have hidden a wrong permission, so they should become assertions.
- **Nine files carry a private copy of the comment stripper** now shared as
  `tests/Support/StripsSourceComments.php`. Consolidating them is mechanical and would have made
  the fifth instance of that bite impossible; it touches nine ratchets at once, so it is its own
  change.
- **`resources/views/order/show.blade.php` renders `{{ $order->payment_type }}` raw** and must
  stay that way — see F173's refuted claim. It is a plan-order view and `for('Bank Transfer')`
  returns null, so "fixing" it would replace a correct label with a dash.

## Count drift in this ledger — measured 2026-10-29, and what it does and does not mean

Two independent read-only audits were run over the `P2-01`, `P2-04` and `P2-08` rows on the owner's
instruction that stale rows be corrected **from real commits and tests, not commit titles**. The
headline is worth stating plainly because it is the opposite of what the instruction anticipated:

- **Zero named artifacts are missing.** Every one of ~100 paths named across both slices resolves,
  and every named PHP/JS artifact passes `php -l` / `node --check`.
- **Zero statuses overstate.** No row marked DONE names a missing artifact or an absent test.
- **The drift runs the other way.** Four status words *understated* what is in the tree
  (P2-01-18, P2-01-19, P2-04-6, and P2-04-8's stale parenthetical — all corrected above), and every
  drifted count is **higher** now than when it was written, because the check suites kept growing.

### Two corrections to how this ledger is read

1. **`P2-08` is not the Flutter parity slice.** It is a single row, *Integration and final
   acceptance*. Flutter parity is **`P2-07`** (`P2-07-12`…`P2-07-15`). A brief that asked for
   "P2-08 (Flutter parity)" was scoped wrong, and anyone re-running that audit should target
   `P2-07`.
2. **The Flutter app repository is checked out in this environment**, at `/home/user/StoreSyria_app98`.
   Rows naming its files (e.g. `P2-04-10`) are directly verifiable and were verified; they must not
   be recorded as "other repo, cannot check".

### The counts that drifted, and why most of them are not errors

A figure like "100 PASSED" is a **run output recorded at a commit**, not a ratchet. Where it matched
the file at its own commit it was correct when written and the row simply was not revisited:

| row | claimed | now | reconciles at its own commit? |
|---|---|---|---|
| P2-01-6 | 15 components | 24 | **yes** — exactly 15 at `40195fa0` |
| P2-01-6 | 70 Phase 02 checks | 159 | **no** — 75 at `40195fa0`; a real `70 PASSED` run is recorded in the evidence doc but matches no inspectable state of the file |
| P2-01-8 | 100 PASSED | 159 | **yes** — exactly 100 at `c5bbff89` |
| P2-01-11 | 137 browser checks | 159 (142 excluding the P2-02 section added in the same commit) | **no** — and `browser-checks-p02.cjs` is unchanged since this row's own commit `99a55a45`, so the figure reconciles to nothing |
| P2-01-12 | 8 `ar.json` entries changed, 0 removed | 9 changed, 0 removed | "0 removed" exact; the 9th line restates a sentence rather than fixing a sense, which is probably the discrepancy |
| P2-01-15 | 34 live checks | 36–38 | **no** — 19 sites × 2 languages, one conditional; 34 is below the static minimum |
| P2-01-16 | measured across 3,433 lines | 3,686 | **yes** — exactly 3,433 at `dcbb549f` |
| P2-01-18 | 48 checks | 123 | the row says the script was "extended" for D-24a and gives no post-extension total, so 48 reads as current when it is historical |
| P2-04-11 | 16 + 4 = 20 new tests | 17 (19 executed) + 5 = 22 | the two extras are the ones this row's own appendix says it added |
| P2-04-12 | 12, amended to 14 | 17 | three above even the amended figure — growth, not shortfall |
| P2-04-12 | `OrderDocumentAccessTest` "twelve cases" | 45 | understated |

**The three worth acting on are the ones that reconcile to nothing** — P2-01-6's 70, P2-01-11's 137
and P2-01-15's 34 — because a figure that was never true cannot be explained by drift. They are
recorded here rather than silently replaced: the suites they describe are run outputs, and
re-deriving them means re-running the browser harness, which is a separate act from this audit.

**Exactly measured and worth keeping as the pattern to copy:** P2-01-9 (21/21), P2-01-10 (17/17,
7/7), P2-01-13 (10/10), P2-01-14 (105 sections, 24 configurations, 10 tests), P2-01-19 (every one of
five figures, including `19 → 0` nested dialogs across 16 views), P2-01-20, P2-01-21 (128/83/0 against
the tree now), P2-04-3 (9/9), P2-04-9 (19 + 10 = 29 exactly, plus the census 94→95 and 57→58 asserted
in the test itself), P2-04-14 (whose apparent shortfall resolves exactly once data providers are
expanded: 3 methods + 6 provider rows = 9, 3 + 4 = 7), P2-08 (`expected_failures: 2`,
`expected_skips: 17`, Contract 26 — all exact).

### One stale-reading hazard, recorded not changed

`P2-01-2`, `-3`, `-4` and `-5` are marked `DONE (built)` with evidence columns saying "not yet
driven". All four **are** now driven, by `browser-checks-p02.cjs:302-442` under `P2-01-9`. The
qualifier was honest when written; left as is, it invites someone to redo work already done.

Two further notes: `P2-01-9`'s `tools/previews/components.blade.php` is under
`docs/development/phase-2/tools/`, while the adjacent `P2-01-7` uses a bare `tools/` to mean
